title: Scandal, sin and why stay
tagline: An honest look at abuse, corrupt leaders and a Church that is holy and full of sinners.
whyItMatters: For many people, scandal is the real reason they left or doubt. They need truth, accountability and compassion, not slogans.

mindset.tip: Listen first. Anger and grief at abuse are fair responses; do not rush to defend. (Psalm 34:18)
Put survivors before the Church’s image. The popes themselves have said so.
Do not minimise or change the subject. Admit failures plainly, then explain why you still stay. (CCC 827)
Never claim more than you know; point people to proper help and reporting where needed. (CCC 2285)

levels.goal: Face the problem and hear honest reasons for staying.

resources.title: Letter to the People of God (2018)
resources.creator: Pope Francis
resources.why: The pope names abuse, cover-up and clericalism and calls the whole Church to penance.

resources.title: Why Remain Catholic? (With So Much Scandal)
resources.creator: Bishop Robert Barron
resources.why: A bishop faces the scandal squarely and gives his reasons for staying.

resources.title: How Should Catholics Respond to Church Scandals?
resources.creator: Catholic Answers
resources.why: A pastoral talk on anger, trust and what to do next.

resources.title: “Why do I stay?” A young Catholic feminist on a church plagued by scandal
resources.creator: Delaney Coyne (America)
resources.why: A lay woman’s honest account of anger, loyalty and the call to reform.
resources.note: America Magazine; a personal essay that includes calls for change.

resources.title: Pastoral Letter to the Catholics of Ireland (2010)
resources.creator: Pope Benedict XVI

resources.title: Vos estis lux mundi
resources.creator: Pope Francis

resources.title: The John Jay Report
resources.creator: Catholic World Report

resources.note: Commentary; the report itself is contested on some points.

resources.title: BishopAccountability.org
resources.creator: BishopAccountability.org
resources.why: A survivor-focused archive of documents and data on the abuse crisis.

resources.title: Saints and Sinners: A History of the Popes
resources.creator: Eamon Duffy
resources.why: A leading Catholic historian tells the popes’ story, good and bad, without flinching.
resources.note: Book for purchase (Yale University Press); found in libraries.
